puzzles.title: The moth in the lantern
puzzles.subtitle: The Glasshouse Folio
puzzles.difficultyEvidence: A symmetric 15×15 silhouette breaks into many short runs; row deductions repeatedly unlock paired column fragments before the central body can be confirmed.
puzzles.story: A pressed-wing diagram was hidden inside the Glasshouse folio. Reconstruct the moth from the surviving row and column runs.

puzzles.title: The divided annunciator
puzzles.subtitle: The West Signal Room
puzzles.difficultyEvidence: An 8×8 balance uses sparse marks, distinct-line constraints and paired no-triple deductions to carry the final third of the grid.
puzzles.story: Restore the divided annunciator. Every row and column must contain four marks of each kind, no three identical marks may touch, and no two complete lines may match.

puzzles.title: The ascending register
puzzles.subtitle: The Observatory Accounts
puzzles.difficultyEvidence: Six sparse givens intersect a long, branching inequality network; no row resolves in isolation and several late placements depend on cross-column order bounds.
puzzles.story: Complete the observatory register with one of each value in every row and column. Each sign records the surviving order between neighbouring entries.

puzzles.title: The lantern vault
puzzles.subtitle: The Lower Arcade
puzzles.difficultyEvidence: A 7×7 vault leaves only a handful of numbered walls; overlapping visibility corridors and exact wall counts force a chain of lamps across all four quadrants.
puzzles.story: Place lanterns through the lower arcade so every open tile is lit, no two lanterns see one another, and each numbered wall receives exactly its stated neighbours.

puzzles.title: The orchard encampment
puzzles.subtitle: The North Garden
puzzles.difficultyEvidence: Ten tree–tent pairings cross a 7×7 orchard; line totals, diagonal exclusions and a late matching bottleneck prevent local greedy placement.
puzzles.story: Place one tent beside each tree in the north garden. Tents may not touch, even diagonally, and the row and column totals must all match.

puzzles.title: The nine flood chambers
puzzles.subtitle: The River Archive
puzzles.difficultyEvidence: Nine irregular reservoirs share seven row and seven column totals; several tanks span four heights, so waterlines must be compared globally rather than solved tank by tank.
puzzles.story: Set the waterline in each flood chamber. Water fills every square at a tank’s chosen height and below, while all row and column totals must match.

puzzles.title: The forty-nine relays
puzzles.subtitle: The City Switchboard
puzzles.difficultyEvidence: A lock-free 7×7 spanning network uses every tile; edge propagation begins the solve, but repeated tees and bends require connectivity reasoning through the central switchboard.
puzzles.story: Rotate every relay until all forty-nine tiles form one closed signal network with no line pointing off the board or into a blank edge.

puzzles.title: The thirty-sixth step
puzzles.subtitle: The Upper Stacks
puzzles.difficultyEvidence: Only a small set of anchors remains on a 6×6 Hamilton path; parity, Manhattan distance and forced-neighbour chains carry long stretches before the final route closes.
puzzles.story: Trace one continuous numbered route through all thirty-six stack tiles. Consecutive values share an edge and every tile is used exactly once.

puzzles.title: The drowned colonnade
puzzles.subtitle: The Tidal Court
puzzles.difficultyEvidence: A fifteen-island sightline graph contains cycles and mutually crossing route options; degree totals leave alternatives until connectivity and crossing exclusions force the final doubles.
puzzles.story: Restore the drowned colonnade. Connect all islands into one network, meet every island count, use no more than two bridges per route and never let bridges cross.
